title: Errata
text:
After the 12th printing
These corrections are not yet reflected in the January 2017 online edition.







Page / location
Correction




8, line −6
“successfully”


12, line +4
If X includes a column of 1s, we have an affine set; if not, we have a hyperplane.


24, line −14
“accuracy as function(s) in low…”


47, line 16
The linear-model assumption is also needed for the scale estimate to be unbiased.


55, below (3.30)
Gamma is a unit upper-triangular matrix, with 1s on the diagonal.


66, near top
U is not square; it has orthonormal columns but is not orthogonal.


85, above (3.70)
Use “a generalized inverse.” In (3.71), Pm is not an orthogonal projection operator.


89, line −5
The first case should have N > p.


161, above §5.6
The CV curve is below, not above, the EPE curve.


193, last line
“multiples” should be “multiplies.”


213, (6.31)
The denominator index should be different from i.


224, (7.12)
Function f should carry superscript p.


301 and 326
Test error for GAM should be 5.5%, not 5.3%.


313–314
The displayed bands are one standard error; the one-SE rule gives 21 terminal nodes, while 17 was selected where the curve flattens.


371, line 6
There are 20,640 rows, not 20,460.


390, line 8
The function does not change in the direction perpendicular to (1,1)T.


397
Robbins and Monro; use 1951 in the references and author index.


509–510, (14.31)–(14.33)
W(C) needs 1/Nk after the first sum; Nk then disappears from the following expressions, giving the correct K-means objective.


517, line −12
China, not Chile.


528, final paragraph
“smallest,” not “largest”; continue until the difference becomes positive, not negative.


548–550
“separate two groups” should be “separate three groups.”


574, (14.104)
Add a constraint such as YTY = I to avoid the trivial solution Y = 0.


579
Bold L should be bold I; “von Luxburg” is the correct spelling.


585, Ex. 14.24(b)
Assume the sum of all xij is 1, or change the definition of c.


639, (17.31)
Use PrΘ(X = xi), not PrΘ(Xi = xi).


713, Huber (1964)
The volume is 35, not 53.



Thanks to the readers who reported these corrections. Contributor names and all earlier-printing errata remain available on the complete legacy errata page while the historical groups are converted to structured content.
The separate K-means explanation remains available.

title: The book
text:
Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani, and Jerome Friedman (Springer, 2009), 763 pages.
The book develops the important ideas in statistical learning in a common conceptual framework, emphasizing concepts and examples. The second edition adds graphical models, random forests, ensemble methods, least-angle regression and lasso path algorithms, non-negative matrix factorization, spectral clustering, and methods for wide data.

title: The Elements of Statistical Learning
text:
About the book
The second edition brings together the important ideas of statistics, data mining, machine learning, and bioinformatics in a common conceptual framework. Its coverage spans supervised and unsupervised learning, including neural networks, support vector machines, trees, boosting, random forests, graphical models, and methods for wide data.

“…a beautiful book.” — David Hand, Biometrics
